snapshots.alt: Tutorial Set 2, Question 3. The present air traffic volume at an airport (number of landings and take offs) during the peak hour is a normal variate with a mean of 200 and a standard deviation of 60 airplanes (See figure).

Question 3 diagram. Vertical axis: Peak Air Traffic. Horizontal axis: Time, years, with 0 and 10 marked. A normal distribution at year 0 is labelled N(200,60). A rising dotted line is labelled Mean Growth Curve.
(a) If the present-runway capacity (for landings and take offs) is 350 planes per hr, what is the current daily probability of air traffic congestion? Assume there is one peak hour daily.

(b) If no additional airports or expansion is built, what would be the probability of congestion 10 years hence? Assume that the mean traffic volume is increasing linearly at 10% of current volume per year, and the coefficient of variation remains the same.
(c) If the projected growth is correct, what airport capacity will be required 10 years from now to maintain the present service condition (i.e. the same probability of congestion as now)?

Tutorial Set 2, Question 4. A system of storm sewers is proposed for a city. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the sewer system in preventing flooding of the streets, the following information has been gathered. The left figure shows the probability mass function for the number of occurrences of rainstorm each year in the city. The right figure shows the distribution of the maximum runoff rate in each storm, which is log-normal with a median of 7 cfs (cubic feet/sec) and COV of 15%. From hydraulic analysis, the proposed sewer system is shown to be adequate for any storm with runoff rate less than 8 cfs. Assume that the maximum runoff rates between storms are statistically independent.

Question 4 diagrams. Left figure: rainstorm probability mass function, with vertical axis P_N(n) and horizontal axis n, number of rainstorms in a year. The probabilities for n=0, 1, 2, and 3 are 0.3, 0.4, 0.2, and 0.1 respectively. Right figure: maximum runoff rate distribution, with vertical axis f_R(r) and horizontal axis r, maximum runoff rate in cfs. A right-skewed density curve is labelled Log Normal Median = 7, c.o.v = 15%.
(a) What is the mean and variance of the number of rain storms in a year for the city? (b) What is the probability of flooding during a rainstorm? (c) What is the probability of flooding in a year?

Tutorial Set 2, Question 8. The cantilever beam shown below is subjected to a random concentrated load P and a random distributed load W. Assume P is normally distributed with mean 5 and standard deviation 1, in kips, and W is normally distributed with mean 1 and standard deviation 0.2, in kips per foot. (a) Determine the mean and variance of the applied bending moment, M = 50W + 10P. Assume that the correlation between W and P is 0.5. (b) The resisting moment of the beam R is Gaussian, with mean 200 and standard deviation 50, in foot-kips. Determine the probability of failure of the beam, P(R < M), assuming that R and M are independent. Diagram: a 10-foot cantilever fixed at the left end, carrying a downward uniformly distributed load W and a downward concentrated load P at the right end, with bending moment M_a at the fixed support.
